sections.name: Spinal cord, roots and spinal nerves

ns-organization.title: Organization of the nervous system
ns-organization.alt: Tree diagram of the nervous system: the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord) and the peripheral nervous system (cranial and spinal nerves and their branches). The peripheral system divides into the autonomic system (heart muscle, smooth muscle, glands) and the somatic system (voluntary skeletal muscles). The autonomic system divides into the parasympathetic division, 'rest and digest', and the sympathetic division, 'active and alert'.

divisions.title: Divisions of the nervous system
divisions.alt: The brain and spinal cord on the left as the central nervous system. On the right, the peripheral nervous system: an afferent division (somatic, visceral and special sensory) and an efferent division (somatic motor and autonomic motor: sympathetic, parasympathetic, enteric).

neuron-synapse.title: A neuron and its synapse
neuron-synapse.alt: Two neurons in series with the nucleus, dendrites, cell body, axon, myelin sheath and synapses labeled. An inset enlarges one synapse: direction of nerve impulse, postsynaptic neuron, mitochondrion, vesicles of transmitter substance, synaptic cleft and receptors on the postsynaptic membrane.

neuron-types.title: Multipolar motor and pseudounipolar sensory neurons
neuron-types.alt: (A) A multipolar motor neuron with its cell body in the CNS and its axon running into the PNS toward an effector organ. (B) A pseudounipolar sensory neuron with its cell body beside the axon, a common stem, and central and peripheral processes running between the CNS and a receptor organ. Labels include dendrites, nucleus, Schwann cell, nodes of the myelin sheath and direction of conduction.

schwann.title: Myelinated and unmyelinated fibers
schwann.alt: A neuron with a myelinated axon: dendrites, cell body, nucleus, axon, unmyelinated region, myelinated internode, neurolemma (Schwann) cell nucleus and myelin. A second view shows a single Schwann cell engulfing several unmyelinated nerve fibers.

nerve-anatomy.title: Anatomy of a nerve
nerve-anatomy.alt: A nerve cut open to show epineurium, perineurium, a fascicle, a peripheral (myelinated) nerve fiber, endoneurium, the blood vessels supplying the nerve (vasa nervorum), the myelin sheath gap (node of Ranvier), the myelin sheath formed by Schwann cells, and the axon.

spinal-nerves-31.title: Spinal and cranial nerves
spinal-nerves-31.alt: Lateral and anterior views of the brain, spinal cord and nerves, color-coded by region: spinal nerves (31 pairs) as cervical (8), thoracic (12), lumbar (5), sacral (5) and coccygeal (1), and cranial nerves (12 pairs) I to XII. Also labeled: cervical and lumbar enlargements of the spinal cord, spinal ganglia and cranial ganglia.

spinal-nerve.title: A spinal nerve
spinal-nerve.alt: A spinal cord segment with its spinal nerve: posterior root, spinal (sensory) ganglion, posterior ramus, anterior root, anterior ramus, a cutaneous nerve to the skin (dermatome) and a motor nerve to skeletal muscle (myotome).

cord-roots.title: Spinal cord segment, roots and rami
cord-roots.alt: A spinal cord segment with the posterior and anterior horns of gray matter, posterior and anterior rootlets, the posterior (sensory) root, the anterior (motor) root, the spinal (sensory) ganglion, the denticulate ligament, the spinal nerve and its posterior and anterior rami.

dermatome-embryology.title: Embryological basis of dermatomes and myotomes
dermatome-embryology.alt: (A) Posterior view of an early embryo showing the neural tube, notochord, neural crest, somite, sclerotome, dermatomyotome, epaxial and hypaxial muscles and dermis, and the intermediate and lateral plate mesoderm. (B) A cross-section with the dorsal and ventral primary rami supplying epaxial and hypaxial muscles. (C) Left lateral view of an embryo with occipital, cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral and coccygeal myotomes.

dermatome-map.title: Dermatome map
dermatome-map.alt: Anterior and posterior views of the body colored by dermatome, from C2 at the back of the head down to L5 and S1 at the foot, with S3 to Co around the anus.

plexuses.title: Somatic nerve plexuses
plexuses.alt: Posterior view of the spinal cord and spinal nerves with the cervical plexus, brachial plexus, intercostal and subcostal nerves, lumbar plexus and sacral plexus and their main nerves labeled. In this figure the cervical plexus is labeled C1 to C5.

cranial-nerves-base.title: Cranial nerves on the base of the brain
cranial-nerves-base.alt: Ventral view of the brain with the cranial nerves drawn in yellow. The visible labels are chiasm, uncus, pons, pyramid and spinal cord; most label lines are blank.

referred-pain.title: Referred pain from the heart
referred-pain.alt: Left: a visceral sensory nerve from the heart and a somatic sensory nerve enter the same spinal cord segment, and the patient perceives diffuse pain in the T1 to T4 dermatomes. Right: a body map of referred pain areas for the heart and other organs.

ans-neurons.title: Sensory, somatic motor and autonomic motor neurons
ans-neurons.alt: Anterior view of the spinal cord with three neuron types in the PNS: a pseudounipolar sensory neuron with its spinal (posterior root) ganglion; a somatic multipolar motor neuron running from the anterior root to an effector organ; and autonomic multipolar motor neurons, with a presynaptic neuron, a synapse within an autonomic ganglion and a postsynaptic neuron running to a gland or smooth muscle.

sympathetic-levels.title: Sympathetic outflow, T1 to L2(3)
sympathetic-levels.alt: A spinal cord cross-section showing the intermediolateral cell columns (lateral horn) between the posterior and anterior horns, beside a chart of spinal levels T1 to L2(3) and the body wall, limb and visceral structures each level supplies: head, salivary glands, eye, heart, lungs, esophagus, stomach, liver, gallbladder, pancreas, small intestine, appendix, colon, kidney, suprarenal gland, rectum, bladder and uterus.

sympathetic-chain.title: Sympathetic trunks and ganglia
sympathetic-chain.alt: (A) Anterior view of the sympathetic trunks beside the vertebral column, with the cervical (superior, middle, inferior), thoracic, lumbar and sacral paravertebral ganglia, the ganglion impar, rami communicantes, splanchnic nerves, and the celiac, superior mesenteric, aorticorenal and inferior mesenteric prevertebral ganglia around the aorta. (B) Anterior oblique view of one spinal cord segment with its roots, rami, rami communicantes, paravertebral and prevertebral ganglia and splanchnic nerves.

prevertebral.title: Prevertebral (preaortic) ganglia
prevertebral.alt: The abdominal aorta with its prevertebral (preaortic) ganglia labeled: the celiac ganglia, superior mesenteric ganglia, aorticorenal ganglia and inferior mesenteric ganglion.

rami-communicantes.title: White and gray rami communicantes
rami-communicantes.alt: A spinal cord segment, spinal nerve and sympathetic chain ganglion. A preganglionic axon leaves the cord and reaches the chain ganglion through the white ramus communicans; a postganglionic axon returns to the spinal nerve through the gray ramus communicans.

sympathetic-courses.title: Courses taken by sympathetic fibers
sympathetic-courses.alt: Anterolateral view of the sympathetic trunk and paravertebral ganglia beside the spinal cord, with the intermediolateral cell column, white and gray rami communicantes, and the four courses taken by presynaptic sympathetic fibers within the trunk: ascend then synapse, synapse at the level of entry, descend then synapse, or pass through to an abdominopelvic splanchnic nerve. Targets include the head, body wall (vasomotion, sudomotion, pilomotion), thoracic viscera, lower limb and abdominopelvic viscera.

sympathetic-overview.title: Sympathetic trunks and their targets
sympathetic-overview.alt: The brain and spinal cord with the two sympathetic trunks of paravertebral ganglia joined at the ganglion impar. Sympathetic nerves follow somatic nerves to the periphery (glands, smooth muscle). Other pathways run through the esophageal plexus to the heart and through the prevertebral plexus to the abdominal and pelvic viscera.

parasympathetic.title: Parasympathetic outflow
parasympathetic.alt: The base of the brain with the cranial parasympathetic outflow through four cranial nerves (III, VII, IX, X) and the ciliary, pterygopalatine, otic and submandibular ganglia, and the sacral parasympathetic outflow from S2 to S4 through the pelvic splanchnic nerves. Targets include the eye, glands of the head, heart, lungs, liver, stomach, pancreas, intestines, bladder and genital organs. The enteric nervous system is also shown.

parasympathetic-ganglia.title: Cranial parasympathetic ganglia
parasympathetic-ganglia.alt: The brain and spinal cord with the cranial parasympathetic outflow: CN III to the ciliary ganglion, CN VII to the pterygopalatine ganglion, CN IX to the otic ganglion, the submandibular ganglion, and CN X to the thoracic and abdominal viscera. The sacral outflow from S2 to S4 supplies the pelvic viscera. Targets include the lacrimal gland, pupil, parotid gland, salivary glands, heart and abdominal and pelvic viscera.

cards.t: Structural divisions of the nervous system
cards.d: The central nervous system (CNS) and the peripheral nervous system (PNS).

cards.t: Functional divisions of the peripheral nervous system
cards.d: The afferent (sensory) division and the efferent (motor) division.
The brain and spinal cord.
All neural structures outside the CNS: the cranial nerves, spinal nerves and their branches.
Transmits sensory input from somatic, visceral and special sensory receptors to the CNS.
Carries motor output from the CNS to effectors. Has two parts: the somatic nervous system and the autonomic nervous system.
The VOLUNTARY motor system. Supplies skeletal muscles.
The INVOLUNTARY motor system. Regulates cardiac muscle, smooth muscle and glandular tissue. Divided into the sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions.
'Active and alert'; 'fight, flight, or fright'. Energy-expending.
'Rest and digest'. Energy-conserving.

cards.t: Number of neurons from the CNS to an autonomic effector
cards.d: TWO multipolar neurons in series: a preganglionic (presynaptic) neuron with its cell body in CNS gray matter, and a postganglionic (postsynaptic) neuron with its cell body in an autonomic ganglion outside the CNS.
Somatic: ONE motor neuron runs from the CNS to the skeletal muscle. Autonomic: TWO neurons in series, with a synapse in an autonomic ganglion.
Contains the nucleus and the metabolic centers of the neuron.
Receive incoming impulses and carry them toward the cell body.
Conducts nerve impulses AWAY from the cell body toward target effectors or synapses.
Has multiple dendrites and a single axon. Its cell body lies in CNS gray matter or in an autonomic ganglion.
Has a single process that splits into a central process (to the CNS) and a peripheral process (to the receptor organ). Its cell body lies in a sensory ganglion.
Wraps peripheral nerve fibers. Forms the myelin sheath around myelinated fibers; one Schwann cell can also engulf several unmyelinated fibers.
Delicate connective tissue surrounding individual nerve fibers and Schwann cells.
Dense connective tissue sheath enclosing a bundle (fascicle) of nerve fibers.
Thick outer connective tissue sheath that encloses and binds multiple fascicles into a nerve trunk.

cards.t: Connective tissue coverings of a nerve, innermost to outermost
cards.d: Endoneurium (around each fiber), then perineurium (around each fascicle), then epineurium (around the whole nerve).
The blood vessels that nourish nerve fibers and their connective tissue sheaths.
31 pairs, arising bilaterally from 31 spinal cord segments.
8 pairs (C1-C8)
12 pairs (T1-T12)
5 pairs (L1-L5)
5 pairs (S1-S5)
1 pair (Co1)

cards.t: Anterior (ventral) horn of the spinal cord
cards.d: Houses the cell bodies of somatic motor neurons that supply skeletal muscle.

cards.t: Posterior (dorsal) horn of the spinal cord
cards.d: Receives the central processes of incoming sensory neurons.
Found ONLY at spinal cord levels T1-L2/L3. Contains the cell bodies of presynaptic sympathetic neurons.
Contains motor (efferent) fibers exiting the spinal cord.

cards.t: Fiber types in the C1-C8 ventral roots
cards.d: GSE (somatic motor) fibers ONLY.

cards.t: Fiber types in the T1-L2 ventral roots
cards.d: GSE (somatic motor) AND GVE (presynaptic sympathetic) fibers.
Contains sensory (afferent) fibers entering the spinal cord.
Sits on the posterior root. Contains the cell bodies of pseudounipolar sensory neurons.

The posterior (sensory) and anterior (motor) roots unite within or just proximal to the intervertebral foramen to form a MIXED spinal nerve, which immediately divides into a posterior ramus and an anterior ramus.
Supplies the deep back muscles, the synovial joints of the vertebral column and the skin of the back. Posterior rami stay separate and do NOT form major somatic plexuses.
Supplies the skin and muscles of the anterior and lateral trunk and of the upper and lower limbs. Merges with adjacent rami to form the major somatic nerve plexuses.
C1-C4, per the text of slide 20. Heads-up: the plexus figure on slides 19 and 20 is labelled C1-C5.
C5-T1. Supplies the muscles of the upper extremity.
L1-L4
L4-S4
S4-Co1
Conveys touch, pain, temperature and proprioception from skin, fascia, skeletal muscles, joints and bones.
Voluntary motor stimuli to skeletal muscles, EXCEPT muscles derived from the pharyngeal arches.
Sensory input from the internal visceral organs.
Involuntary autonomic motor supply to smooth muscle, cardiac muscle and glands. Comes as presynaptic (preganglionic) and postsynaptic (postganglionic) fibers.
Visual impulses from the retina (CN II) and auditory and vestibular stimuli (CN VIII).
Smell via CN I; taste via CN VII, IX and X.
Motor supply to skeletal muscles derived from the pharyngeal (branchial) arches.
SVE fibers of CN V (trigeminal)
SVE fibers of CN VII (facial)
SVE fibers of CN IX (glossopharyngeal) and CN X (vagus)
SVE fibers of CN X (vagus)
SVE fibers of CN XI (spinal accessory)
SVA fibers of CN X (vagus)
12 pairs (CN I-XII). 11 pairs arise directly from the brain.

cards.t: Cranial nerve that arises from the superior spinal cord
cards.d: CN XI (spinal accessory). The other 11 pairs arise from the brain.
Abducens nerve

cards.t: The 12 cranial nerves, I to XII
cards.d: I olfactory, II optic, III oculomotor, IV trochlear, V trigeminal, VI abducens, VII facial, VIII vestibulocochlear, IX glossopharyngeal, X vagus, XI spinal accessory, XII hypoglossal.
The sympathetic division: presynaptic cell bodies in the spinal cord at T1-L2/L3.

cards.t: Where are the presynaptic (preganglionic) sympathetic cell bodies?
cards.d: ONLY in the intermediolateral cell column (IML, lateral horn) of the spinal cord at T1-L2/L3.

cards.t: Where are the postsynaptic (postganglionic) sympathetic cell bodies?
cards.d: In the paravertebral ganglia (sympathetic trunk) and the prevertebral (preaortic) ganglia.

Linked paravertebral ganglia forming right and left chains beside the vertebral column, along essentially its whole length. The superior cervical ganglion lies at the base of the cranium; the ganglion impar forms where the two trunks unite at the coccyx.
Lie in the plexuses around the origins of the main branches of the abdominal aorta, for which they are named: celiac, superior mesenteric, aorticorenal and inferior mesenteric ganglia.
Carry presynaptic sympathetic (preganglionic GVE) fibers. Found ONLY on spinal nerves T1-L2/L3.
Carry postsynaptic sympathetic (postganglionic GVE) fibers. Connect to ALL 31 pairs of spinal nerves (C1 to Co1).

cards.t: Courses of presynaptic sympathetic fibers in the sympathetic trunk
cards.d: 1) Ascend and synapse in a higher paravertebral ganglion. 2) Descend and synapse in a lower one. 3) Synapse at the level of entry. 4) Pass through WITHOUT synapsing, in an abdominopelvic splanchnic nerve to a prevertebral ganglion.

cards.t: Primary function and effectors of the sympathetic division
cards.d: Innervates ALL body blood vessels (vasomotion, its primary function), sweat glands (sudomotion) and arrector pili muscles of the hair (pilomotion).
The parasympathetic division: presynaptic cell bodies in the brainstem (fibers exit in CN III, VII, IX and X) and in sacral spinal cord segments S2-S4.

cards.t: Cranial parasympathetic outflow: origin and exit
cards.d: Presynaptic cell bodies in brainstem gray matter; fibers exit the CNS in cranial nerves III, VII, IX and X.

cards.t: Cranial parasympathetic outflow: what it supplies
cards.d: CN III, VII and IX supply structures of the head. CN X (vagus) supplies the thoracic and abdominal viscera.

cards.t: Sacral parasympathetic outflow: origin and exit
cards.d: Presynaptic cell bodies in sacral spinal cord gray matter at S2-S4; fibers exit through the sacral spinal nerves S2-S4.

cards.t: Sacral parasympathetic outflow: what it supplies
cards.d: The GI tract from the descending colon to the rectum, and the pelvic viscera.

cards.t: Where are the postsynaptic (postganglionic) parasympathetic cell bodies?
cards.d: In four pairs of cranial parasympathetic ganglia, or in intramural (terminal) ganglia in or on the wall of the target organ.
Ciliary, pterygopalatine, otic and submandibular.
Cranial parasympathetic ganglion that connects with the oculomotor nerve (CN III).
Cranial parasympathetic ganglion that connects with the facial nerve (CN VII).
Cranial parasympathetic ganglion that connects with the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX).
Cranial parasympathetic ganglion that connects with the facial nerve (CN VII).
Very LONG presynaptic fibers (from the CNS all the way to the effector organ) and very SHORT postsynaptic fibers (from a ganglion near or in the organ).
The unilateral area of skin supplied by the sensory fibers of a single spinal nerve pair.
The unilateral mass of muscle supplied by the motor fibers of a single spinal nerve pair.

cards.t: Embryological basis of dermatomes and myotomes
cards.d: The relationship between spinal nerves and the tissue derived from the dermatomyotome (skin and muscle) remains throughout life.
Back of the head; the 'highest' dermatome of the body.
Top part of the shoulder
Thumb
Middle finger
Little finger
Level of the nipples
Level of the umbilicus (navel)
Skin along the inguinal crease
Big toe, per the text of slide 18. Heads-up: the map on slide 17 shows the big toe within L5.
Little toe and sole of the foot
Skin around the anus

cards.t: Why is there no C1 dermatome?
cards.d: Spinal nerve C1 lacks a significant afferent (sensory) component, so it does not supply skin.

Pain perceived at a somatic location distant from the involved visceral organ. Visceral and somatic sensory fibers enter the same spinal cord segment, so the CNS interprets the pain as coming from the area that segment innervates.

cards.t: The two types of referred pain
cards.d: Viscero-somatic and somato-somatic.

cards.d: T1-T4 dermatomes
